Article Title: In 2017, a few volunteers packed 10 backpacks with food for children; nine years later, the programme is feeding thousands of students across Metro Atlanta
Article Text:
Image: Backpack Buddies of Metro Atlanta

How Backpack Buddies started with 10 backpacks

From one school to dozens: How the programme scaled up

Ronald and Samra Robbins, founders of Backpack Buddies of Metro Atlanta, receive the Max & Mary London People Power Award from Jewish Federation of Greater Atlanta President & CEO Eric Robbins. (Image: Patti with Scensarions)

What goes into a weekend meal, and how the model works

The role of volunteers and what comes next

Backpack Buddies of Metro Atlanta began in 2017 with a small group of volunteers at a single local elementary school, packing nonperishable food for children who faced food insecurity over the weekend. The first distribution served just 10 students. Nine years later, the organisation provides weekend meals to thousands of children across dozens of schools throughout metro Atlanta. Here's how a small volunteer effort grew into a regional programme, and what it takes to keep it running today. It was founded by Ronald and Samra Robbins.The programme's story began at one local elementary school, where volunteers gathered each week to pack nonperishable food for children facing weekend food insecurity. According to the Backpack Buddies of Metro Atlanta, the bags were discreetly delivered to the school so students could take food home in their backpacks without drawing attention to their circumstances. The idea behind it was simple, if children couldn't rely on school meals over the weekend, the community could help make sure food was available at home. That first distribution reached just 10 students, laying the groundwork for what would grow far beyond a single school.Backpack Buddies became a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit in 2022, and during the 2022–2023 school year, it was feeding approximately 800 children across 27 schools. By the start of the 2025–2026 school year, that number had grown to 2,625 children across 53 schools, supported by hundreds of volunteers and 34 Community Buddy organisations. In April 2025, the organisation reached another milestone, delivering its one millionth meal, a figure representing years of food sourcing, inventory management, packing, transportation and school partnerships working together behind the scenes.Backpack Buddies provides shelf-stable, kid-friendly food designed specifically for children to have access to meals and snacks over the weekend, including proteins and mains, vegetables, breakfast items, fruits, snacks and drinks. The goal isn't simply to put food into a backpack, but to give children reliable access to food during the days when school meals aren't available. The model relies heavily on Community Buddies, organisations such as religious groups, civic organisations and senior centres that adopt one or more schools and help pack and deliver meals to children identified as needing weekend food assistance.Volunteers remain central to the programme's operations, helping inventory food, prepare orders, load deliveries and support community events at the organisation's Dunwoody warehouse. As Backpack Buddies has grown, so does its need for volunteer support, since a larger programme means more food to move, more orders to prepare and more schools to serve. The organisation estimates that $250 can feed one child every weekend of the school year, and continues to rely on donations, volunteers and new Community Buddy partnerships to keep expanding its reach across metro Atlanta, where the need for weekend food support has continued to grow alongside the programme itself.
Article Summary: Backpack Buddies of Metro Atlanta began in 2017 with a small group of volunteers. The first distribution served just 10 students at a local elementary school. Nine years later, the organisation provides weekend meals to thousands of children across dozens of schools throughout metro Atlanta. In April 2025, it delivered its one millionth meal.

Article Title: Apple Siri settlement: iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 16 owners can now claim up to $95; here's how to file
Article Text:
Only US buyers of seven iPhone models qualify for the payout

Filing an Apple Siri settlement claim needs your iPhone serial number

Claims close on December 21, but payments will wait until 2027

Apple has opened the claims window for its $250 million (about Rs 2,200 crore) settlement over the delayed Apple Intelligence upgrade to Siri. Eligible iPhone owners in the US can now file for a payout of $25 per device. That figure could rise to $95, depending on how many people come forward.The class action, Landsheft et al. v. Apple Inc., accused the company of selling the iPhone 16 as "built for Apple Intelligence" while the smarter Siri shown at WWDC 2024 was nowhere near ready. That upgraded Siri only reached users with iOS 27 earlier this month, more than two years after its first demo. Apple has denied any wrongdoing, and the settlement terms say it is not an admission of liability.The claim covers purchases made between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025. The iPhone 15 Pro and 15 Pro Max qualify, along with the entire iPhone 16 lineup: the iPhone 16, 16 Plus, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max and the budget iPhone 16e.You must be the original buyer, and the phone must have been bought for personal or work use, not resale. Indian buyers of the same models are not covered, since the case was filed and settled in the US.Claims are filed on the official website, SmartphoneAISettlement.com.The form asks for your name, address, phone number and the iPhone's serial number, which you'll find under Settings > General > About. If you don't have the serial number, the form will take your Apple Account email and the phone number linked to the device instead.Eligible owners should also receive an email over the coming days with a claim ID and PIN. You can still file without them. Each device needs its own claim, and only one payment is allowed per phone.The $95 maximum depends on how many iPhone owners filePayouts start at $25 per device and can climb to $95 if fewer valid claims come in than expected. Payment options include PayPal, Venmo, direct deposit and a paper check.Ryan Clarkson, co-lead counsel on the case and founder of Clarkson Law Firm, described the fund as the largest false advertising settlement on record.The deadline to file is December 21, 2026. A federal district court in San Jose will hold the final approval hearing on February 24, 2027, and payments will only go out after that. Any appeal could delay them further.Anyone unsure about eligibility can call the settlement administrator on 1-888-988-8945. For those who bought an iPhone 16 waiting for the new Siri, the money will arrive even later than the feature did.
Article Summary: Claims close on December 21, but payments will wait until 2027. Only US buyers of seven iPhone models qualify for the payout. Each device needs its own claim, and only one payment is allowed per phone. Payment options include PayPal, Venmo, direct deposit and a paper check.

Article Title: How to find your lost Android phone using Google Find Hub
Article Text:
Representative Image

Set up Find Hub on your Android phone before you lose it

Location and Bluetooth are turned on

"Allow device to be located" is enabled under the Find Hub settings (look under Security, or Google > All Services > Personal & Device Safety)

Offline finding is set to "With network in busy places only" or "With network everywhere"

A PIN, pattern or password is set, since offline finding won't work without one

You're signed in to a Google account you can still access

How to locate a lost Android phone on a map

Mark as lost: Locks the phone with your PIN and shows a message and contact number on the lock screen. On phones running Android 17 with fingerprint or Face Unlock, it adds two-step verification too. Keep the message short, as scammers can use those details to trick you into unlocking the phone for them.

Remote Lock: No Google password handy? You can lock the screen using just your phone number.

Factory reset: Your last resort. It permanently deletes everything and removes the phone from Find Hub, so you can't track it after that.

Lost your Android phone? Google's Find Hub is the first place to check, and you don't need a second Android device to use it. Any web browser, on a laptop or a friend's iPhone, can show you where your phone was last seen, make it ring, lock it, or wipe it clean.Find Hub is the new name for Google's Find My Device. It runs on an opt-in network of millions of Android devices that pick up Bluetooth signals from lost phones, earbuds and tracker tags, then quietly report their location back to the owner. That location data is end-to-end encrypted, so only you can see it. Google says it can't either.Find Hub switches on automatically once you sign in with a Google account. But a few settings decide how useful it will be on the day your phone goes missing. Check these now:Newer Pixel phones can even be located several hours after they've been switched off. Menu names vary a little by brand, but the options look similar on most Android phones.Open the Find Hub app on another Android phone or a Wear OS watch, or visit the Find Hub website on any browser. Sign in with the same Google account and pick your phone from the device list. The map shows its last known location, and you can get directions through Google Maps.If the phone is somewhere nearby, tap Play sound. It rings at full volume for five minutes, even on silent. Within 10 metres, the Find Nearby feature shows a shape that fills in as you get closer.Lock or erase your Android phone if it's stolenIf the phone is gone for good, act fast.Check those settings once, and the next time your phone goes missing, you'll know exactly where to look.
Article Summary: Find Hub is the new name for Google's Find My Device. It runs on an opt-in network of millions of Android devices. Location data is end-to-end encrypted, so only you can see it. Newer Pixel phones can be located several hours after they've been switched off.

Article Title: Meta unveils camera-free Ray-Ban Audio glasses and a keychain AI companion at Connect 2026
Article Text:
Ray-Ban Meta Audio : cameras out, all-day wearability in

Muse Charm: an AI agent you can put on a keychain

At its annual Meta Connect event, Facebook-parent Meta has announced a major expansion of its consumer hardware portfolio with the launch of new Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses and a quirky Muse AI keychain. The new products unveiled highlight Meta’s AI push to embed AI agents into everyday life simply by blending fashion, utility and entertainment. The new Ray-Ban Meta glasses lineup builds on Meta’s partnership with EssilorLuxottica. The glasses now feature deeper AI integration, including voice-controlled access to Meta’s AI assistant, improved audio quality, and enhanced camera capabilities. On the other hand, Meta Muse AI keychain is a pocket-sized device described as “Tamagotchi-like.” The gadget acts as a portable AI agent, offering playful interactions, reminders, and personalized assistance. Meta positioned Muse as a way to make AI more approachable, turning everyday tasks into engaging experiences.The headline hardware announcement was Ray-Ban Meta Audio, Meta's first-ever camera-free smart glasses, developed through its ongoing partnership with EssilorLuxottica. By ditching the camera setup entirely, Meta managed to bring the glasses down to just 43 grams — noticeably lighter than the roughly 50g standard Ray-Ban Meta models and far lighter than the 70g Display glasses — while still packing in hands-free music and podcast playback, calling, and conversations with Meta's AI assistant.The glasses come in Clubmaster and Burbank styles, with customizable temple tips, nose pads, and overextension hinges for a more tailored fit, and support a wide range of optical prescriptions.Battery life is rated at up to 12 hours on a single charge, extendable to roughly 48 additional hours using the included charging case. Ray-Ban Meta Audio launches October 13 at $349, with pre-orders open now.Meta also used the moment to introduce Hearing Enhancement, an FDA-cleared accessibility feature arriving later this year for supported AI glasses. Using the glasses' six-speaker array, the feature is designed to help people who are hard of hearing pick out speech more clearly in noisy environments, letting users adjust left-right audio balance or shift to mono audio in one ear. Meta is pricing it at $149.99 as a one-time purchase, or bundling it into a Meta One subscription, framing it as a notably more affordable alternative to traditional hearing aids, which the company says typically start around $800. A 30-day free trial will also be available.Beyond the audio-only model, Meta also refreshed its standard Ray-Ban Meta line with the Gen 3 glasses, adding a slimmer build, longer battery life, a 12MP camera, and 3K Ultra HD video recording. The company additionally previewed a new hologram calling feature for Ray-Ban Meta Display users, letting someone do a quick self-capture with their phone to generate a hologram visible to whoever they're calling — expected to arrive in early access on WhatsApp in the US within the next few months.The event's true "one more thing" moment came when CEO Mark Zuckerberg unveiled Muse Charm, a small, palm-sized wearable designed to give people another physical way to interact with Muse, Meta's recently launched and increasingly popular personal AI agent.The device houses a tiny screen displaying Jolly, the cute animated avatar Meta has built to represent Muse, and is meant to be carried in a pocket or clipped onto a keychain. Zuckerberg explained that the team condensed the entire Muse experience — including its real-time voice and avatar system — into a device small enough to live on a keychain while remaining constantly available to talk to. A fingerprint sensor built into the corner of the device lets users start a conversation instantly, without needing to unlock a phone or open an app first. For anyone not wearing AI glasses, Zuckerberg positioned Muse Charm as the fastest possible way to talk to Muse and show it what's happening around you.The gadget leans into a distinctly Tamagotchi-like aesthetic — small, personality-driven, and designed to keep users continually engaged with Meta's AI software. Zuckerberg acknowledged the hardware isn't quite ready for release, saying the team still needs to finalize how its internal components are laid out, but confirmed Muse Charm is on track to ship in time for the December holiday season.
Article Summary: Muse AI keychain is a pocket-sized device described as “Tamagotchi-like” The gadget acts as a portable AI agent, offering playful interactions, reminders, and personalized assistance. Ray-Ban Meta Audio is Meta's first-ever camera-free smart glasses, developed through its partnership with EssilorLuxottica.

Article Title: Boat launches smart earbuds range with Crest AI; offers Airdopes Prime 800 D, Airdopes Prime 701 ANC and Nirvana Ion ANC earbuds
Article Text:
Boat launches smart earbuds range with CREST AI

Boat has launched its first smart audio devices range featuring Boat Crest AI, its AI-powered platform built with Google Gemini. The lineup includes Boat Airdopes Prime 800, Boat Airdopes Prime 701 ANC and Boat Nirvana Ion ANC. With the launch, Boat is introducing a new proposition for personal audio — ‘Intelligent Ears’ — earbuds designed not just for listening, but to listen, understand, converse and assist.In a press release, the company said that the Crest AI is built around a simpler idea: bringing intelligence to something consumers already wear throughout their day — their earbuds. At the heart of the experience are three capabilities — Crest Ask, G- Assist and Crest Translate, or simply: Ask. Assist. Translate.With Crest Ask, users can ask questions, explore ideas, learn and have natural conversations with AI. Instead of repeatedly reaching for a phone or typing a query, users can ask follow-up questions and continue the conversation through their earbuds.With G- Assist take the experience from conversation to action. With integration across Google Gmail, Tasks, and Calendar, users can access everyday productivity and communication capabilities through voice.From asking the assistant to “summarize my day” to “reply to an email,” G-Assist helps users manage tasks, stay on top of schedules, and interact with their digital routines without reaching for their phones.Crest Translate enables real-time, two-way translation across 25+ languages, helping people speaking different languages communicate more naturally.Gaurav Nayyar, CEO, Boat said “Why should intelligence be limited to our rooms, desks, pockets or screens? We believe it can become much more natural and simply be with you. With Crest AI, built with Google Gemini, we are bringing that intelligence to your ears. Our idea of ‘Intelligent Ears’ is simple: earbuds that can listen, understand, converse and assist. But this is just the beginning, we are working on multiple other use cases. For ten years, Boat has helped India listen. Now, we want to help India listen, understand, converse and assist”.The Boat Airdopes Prime 800 D combines Crest AI capabilities with Dolby Audio and 11mm dynamic drivers tuned to Boat Signature Sound. The earbuds offer up to 45 hours of total playback, Multipoint Connectivity and four microphones with AI-ENx technology, bringing together entertainment, communication and intelligent assistance in one device.Crest AI is also available on the Boat Airdopes Prime 701 ANC and Boat Nirvana Ion ANC. The Boat Airdopes Prime 800 D, Boat Airdopes Prime 701 ANC and Boat Nirvana Ion ANC are available through the Boat website and leading e-commerce platforms.
Article Summary: Boat has launched its first smart audio devices range featuring Boat Crest AI, its AI-powered platform built with Google Gemini. At the heart of the experience are three capabilities — Crest Ask, G- Assist and Crest Translate. With the launch, Boat is introducing a new proposition for personal audio — 'Intelligent Ears'

Article Title: Motorola showcases Signature 27 with 50MP main camera and 200MP periscope telephoto camera
Article Text:
Motorola launches Signature 27 with 50MP main camera and 200MP periscope telephoto camera

Motorola Signature 27 features

Motorola Signature 27 operating system

Motorola has showcased the Signature 27, its second smartphone in the Signature series and one of the first phones announced with Qualcomm’s latest Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset. The smartphone was unveiled at the Snapdragon Summit 2026 on Tuesday and comes with a 50MP Sony LYTIA 910 main camera and a 200MP periscope telephoto camera. Motorola is also changing its naming system with this phone, using the final two digits of the upcoming year for its new generations. The company has not yet announced the price or exact sale date, but says the Signature 27 will launch globally later this year.The Motorola Signature 27 is powered by Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor. Motorola says the chipset brings improvements to on-device AI, camera performance, gaming response and download speeds. The phone also comes with Motorola’s ArcticMesh cooling system. It combines diamond-infused thermal gel, liquid metal and copper mesh with a redesigned 3D vapour chamber. Motorola says the new vapour chamber is 40% larger than the previous generation.Motorola Signature 27 gets a 50MP Sony LYTIA 910 main camera along with a 200MP periscope telephoto camera.Motorola has also introduced its Video Enhancement Engine, which uses AI to study a scene before and during video recording and adjust colour tones in real time.The phone will also support Google's Gemini Omni, which can use prompts, photos or existing video clips to create a finished video. Google's Lyria can be used to generate music and soundtracks.The phone will be available in Pantone Coal Smoke and Pantone Capulet Green. The Coal Smoke version has a woven texture designed to improve grip and durability, while Capulet Green gets a brushed, textile-inspired finish.Motorola says the Signature 27 will receive seven years of OS upgrades and is expected to launch with Android 17. It is also the company's first smartphone with Audio by B&O, with the branding etched onto the rear panel.Motorola has not yet revealed the phone's display, battery capacity, charging speed, RAM, storage or other camera sensors. Pricing and the exact launch date are also yet to be announced.
Article Summary: Motorola Signature 27 gets a 50MP Sony LYTIA 910 main camera along with a 200MP periscope telephoto camera. The phone is powered by Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor. Motorola has not yet revealed the phone's display, battery capacity, charging speed, RAM, storage or other camera sensors.

Article Title: AI malware is becoming its own category: Researchers found a malicious program that uses multiple AI models to decide what to do
Article Text:
AI malware is becoming its own category: Researchers found a malicious program that uses multiple AI models to decide what to do

How does the AI-powered malware work

Researchers are finding more AI-powered malware

What the findings suggest

Researchers have reportedly found a malicious program that uses AI model to help decide what it should do next. The malware, called CLOSEDQUORUM, can contact up to four AI models, including DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral and Google Gemini. Instead of relying only on instructions written by its developers, the program asks these AI systems for guidance and uses their responses to decide its next steps. Reported by Wired, the discovery was made by researchers at Cisco Talos, who have also created an open-source framework to track malware that uses AI.CLOSEDQUORUM is designed for Windows and can use several AI services at the same time. Researchers describe the setup as a kind of “hive mind”, because the malware can seek decisions from multiple AI models. If one AI service is unavailable, the others can continue working.As stated in the report, researchers also found no mechanism that would allow a human to step in and control the process.The malware is designed to steal login credentials and cryptocurrency. Researchers also found links to cybercrime forums discussing credit-card fraud dating back to 2025. However, they could not confirm who created CLOSEDQUORUM or whether it has been used in real-world attacks.Cisco Talos created the Cognitive Artifact Intelligence Research Network (CAIRN) after researchers began finding signs that attackers were integrating AI into malware.Ryan Fetterman of Cisco Talos said AI integration leaves behind identifiable “fingerprints” that can help researchers track and classify these programs.“The core idea is that AI integration has these vestiges, like fingerprints, that are left behind... That gives us a signal that we can use to track these samples, classify them, and look at what's happening,” Fetterman said.When Fetterman first searched for AI-integrated malware, he found only around nine named malware families, along with several proof-of-concept examples. After CAIRN was developed, researchers identified about 20 additional examples within a few months.The findings suggest that AI is becoming more deeply integrated into some malware rather than simply being used by hackers to write code or create phishing messages. Matt Olney of Cisco Talos said attackers are now beginning to operationalise AI.“Initially, everyone saw AI as a productivity tool, right?... Now what we're seeing is that it's becoming operationalized.”He said AI could allow attackers to run more campaigns, target more systems and handle different computers because the technology can provide responses and guidance in the background.
Article Summary: Malware can contact up to four AI models, including DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral and Google Gemini. Researchers describe setup as a kind of ‘hive mind’ because the malware can seek decisions from multiple AI models. If one AI service is unavailable, the others can continue working.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works



Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next. The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.

Article Title: Mandals, dhol-tasha troupes will face music for noisy processions: Pune CP
Article Text:
Police will monitor noise levels at 120 locations along the immersion route, with a permanent noise-monitoring station set up at Alka Talkies Chowk.

21 cases in Pune, 50 in

Pimpri Chinchwad

Shirgaon police seize sound system for exceeding decibel limits

Monitoring via centralised system





PUNE: Police commissioner Amitesh Kumar on Wednesday warned that strict action would be taken against both Ganapati mandals and dhol-tasha troupes if they were found violating prescribed noise limits during Friday’s immersion procession.“If the decibel level of dhol-tasha troupes exceeds the permissible limits, we will file cases against them too,” the Pune CP said.Police will monitor noise levels at 120 locations along the immersion route, with a permanent noise-monitoring station set up at Alka Talkies Chowk. “Dedicated teams will continuously track decibel levels throughout the procession. Mandals have been permitted to use a maximum of four top speakers and four bass speakers. If a mandal uses more speakers than permitted, we will seize the entire sound system,” Kumar said.Police will also strictly enforce the ban on plasma speakers, mid-pressure speakers and toll instruments. “While there is no cap on the number of dhols, tashas or troupe members, action will be taken if noise levels breach prescribed limits,” the Pune CP said.During the ongoing Ganesh festival, Pune police have already registered 21 cases against mandals for violating noise pollution norms.In Pimpri Chinchwad, police have registered 50 FIRs against Ganesh mandals and sound system suppliers for exceeding permissible decibel limits.As part of the action, Pimpri Chinchwad police seized loudspeakers, mixers and vehicles from 40 mandals found violating noise regulations. Ahead of the festival, Pimpri Chinchwad police commissioner Vinoy Kumar Choubey and other senior officers held meetings with Ganesh mandal office-bearers, directing them to strictly adhere to prescribed sound limits.“Several mandals complied with the guidelines and refrained from playing loud music during processions. Action was taken only against those found violating permissible noise levels,” a police officer said.Many areas in Pimpri Chinchwad immerse Ganesh idols on the seventh day of the festival. Processions were held on Sept 20 in Sangvi, Dighi, Shirgaon, Talegaon and other localities. Police teams were deployed along immersion routes to monitor noise levels and initiate action against errant mandals and sound suppliers.Pune police said the entire immersion procession would be monitored through a centralised system at Shivajinagar police headquarters, supported by a dedicated war room at Faraskhana police station.Around 3,500 CCTV cameras, aided by AI-based video analytics, will be used for crowd monitoring, people counting, detection of suspicious activities, abandoned objects, violence, smoke and weapons. The system will also feature facial recognition, intelligent video search and incident detection tools.Police will also deploy an Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR)-based system to detect traffic violations like wrong-way driving, triple-seat riding, illegal parking, footpath encroachment and speeding. An IP-based public address system at 250 locations will be used for announcements, crowd management and emergency communication.Five mobile surveillance vehicles and 19 mini-surveillance vehicles equipped with HD cameras, AI analytics and public address systems will be stationed across the old city.Drone surveillance will supplement CCTV feeds from Metro stations, Pune Municipal Corporation cameras and Ganapati mandals. Police will also track mandals in real time through GPS devices installed on procession units.More than 10,000 police personnel, home guards, SRPF jawans and other security staff will be deployed for bandobust duty on Friday and Saturday, Pune CP Kumar said.
Article Summary: Police will monitor noise levels at 120 locations along the immersion route, with a permanent noise-monitoring station set up at Alka Talkies Chowk. Around 3,500 CCTV cameras, aided by AI-based video analytics, will be used for crowd monitoring, people counting and detection of suspicious activities.

Article Title: Australia turns Sydney’s food waste into biogas and electricity; a 62,500-tonne facility can power around 4,000 homes
Article Text:
PC: AI Generated

How Australia turns food waste into a resource at EarthPower

Inside Australia’s EarthPower process for turning waste into power

PC: AI Generated

EarthPower’s annual food waste capacity

The digestion process creates more than electricity at EarthPower

EarthPower collects food waste from across Sydney’s supply chain

EarthPower turns biogas into electricity and useful process heat

Food waste can be recovered instead of simply sent to landfill

62,500 tonnes of food waste feed EarthPower’s recovery system

Every day, food that has reached the end of its useful life leaves kitchens, shops, factories and distribution centres across Sydney. Much of it could end up as waste with little further use. At EarthPower in Camellia, that material takes a different route. The facility uses anaerobic digestion to break down organic food waste and capture the biogas produced along the way. That gas is then used to generate electricity, while the remaining material is processed into a soil improver. According to Waste Management Review 2025, EarthPower's upgraded ‘plate to paddock’ facility has a total capacity of 62,500 tonnes, of which 65% is dedicated to food waste expected to yield roughly 1,500 tonnes of soil improver annually while generating enough electricity to power around 4,000 homes.Australia produces a large amount of municipal waste on a per-person basis, and food makes up a substantial share of it. Food waste is also classed as putrescible waste, meaning it can break down relatively quickly when sent to landfill.EarthPower was established in Sydney’s Camellia suburb as a dedicated alternative for organic waste. Rather than treating discarded food as material with no further purpose, the facility takes in waste from a range of businesses and local government sources and puts the organic content through a recovery process.Its intake is not limited to one type of food waste. Solid organic material, grease trap waste, spadable sludge, organic liquids and selected packaged waste can all form part of the feedstock accepted by the facility.That gives the plant a fairly broad role in the local waste system. Food manufacturers and processors, distributors, retailers, commercial kitchens and other businesses can send material there instead of relying solely on conventional disposal.The central part of the operation takes place inside two anaerobic digesters. There is no need for oxygen in this stage. Bacteria break down the organic material inside the digesters, producing biogas as the waste decomposes. The gas is collected rather than released and is directed towards cogeneration engines. Those engines turn the biogas into electricity. In practical terms, the process takes material that would otherwise have been discarded and extracts energy from it.The electricity does not all leave the site. EarthPower first uses its own energy and gas production to support the facility's operation. Surplus electricity can then be supplied to the grid for use by domestic, commercial and industrial customers.It is a relatively direct chain: food waste enters the plant, microorganisms break down the organic material, biogas is captured, and that gas becomes electricity.EarthPower's capacity changed significantly when the facility underwent major technological upgrades. The improvements increased its annual feedstock capacity to 62,500 tonnes (65% is dedicated to food waste). At that level, the electricity produced can provide enough power for roughly 4,000 homes. The figure is important because the plant is doing more than simply reducing the volume of material requiring disposal. Its output includes an energy product as well as a recovered material that can be used elsewhere. The upgraded capacity also reflects the range of organic waste being handled. Food does not arrive at the site in one consistent form. Some material is solid, some is liquid, and some comes from waste streams such as grease traps or packaged food.Anaerobic digestion does not make the entire material disappear. A nutrient-rich sludge remains after the digestion process. At EarthPower, this material is dried using heat generated by the cogeneration engines before being granulated. It can then be sold into agricultural and horticultural markets as a soil improver.That gives the process a second output beyond electricity. The organic waste is effectively split into useful products: the biogas becomes energy, while the remaining material is prepared for use in soil.For a facility dealing with tens of thousands of tonnes of food waste, that distinction matters. The purpose is not simply to move waste somewhere else. The process is designed to recover value from different parts of the material.The feedstock reaching EarthPower comes from several points along the food supply chain. Food manufacturing and processing businesses can send their organic waste to the facility, as can companies involved in transportation, storage, wholesale and retail distribution. Commercial kitchens and local government are also among the sources.This means the system sits alongside the everyday movement of food through Sydney rather than operating as a plant for a single type of discarded material. A supermarket, commercial kitchen or food processor may generate waste for very different reasons, but much of that material shares the same basic characteristic: it contains organic matter that can be broken down. EarthPower's system is built around making use of that common property.The most interesting part of the process is perhaps how closely its outputs are linked to its own operation. Biogas produced from the incoming waste fuels the cogeneration engines. Those engines generate electricity, but their heat is also useful. Heat from the engines is used to dry the sludge left behind after digestion. That creates a connected system in which the energy produced during treatment helps prepare another recovered product.The electricity generated on site also helps the facility operate before excess power is sent to the wider grid. In this sense, the plant is not simply an electricity generator attached to a waste facility. The two functions are tied together.Landfill remains a conventional destination for food waste, but sending organic material through anaerobic digestion changes what can be recovered from it. EarthPower's process is designed to divert food waste away from landfill while capturing biogas and producing a soil improver. Veolia, which operates the facility, describes the approach as a form of resource recovery in which material that would otherwise be discarded is given another use.For businesses supplying the plant, there is also a practical consideration. Sending food waste for recovery can reduce disposal requirements and associated costs, while the treatment process provides an alternative to fossil-fuel-based energy generation.The result is not a single waste solution but a chain of uses built around the material that remains after food is no longer wanted.After the 2024 upgrades, the EarthPower facility has a total processing capacity of 62,500 tonnes, with Waste Management Review reporting that 65% is dedicated to food waste. The upgraded operation can generate enough green electricity to potentially power around 4,000 local homes.The same process also produces a granulated soil improver for agricultural and horticultural use. So the discarded food arriving at Camellia does not have one final destination. Its organic content is processed into biogas and energy, while the material left after digestion is prepared for another use.For Sydney's food waste, that turns what begins as a disposal problem into a stream from which both energy and recovered material can be taken.
Article Summary: Sydney facility uses anaerobic digestion to break down food waste. The biogas produced along the way is used to generate electricity. The remaining material is processed into a soil improver that can be sold into agricultural and horticultural markets. EarthPower has a total capacity of 62,500 tonnes, of which 65% is dedicated to food Waste.

Article Title: In 2015, Brazilian researchers found whole forests floating through the Amazon; 40-foot trees rooted in 10-foot-deep soil with caimans beneath
Article Text:
AI Representation: Brazilian researchers found whole forests floating through the Amazon. Image credits: Chatgpt

Matupás form from decades of accumulated vegetation

Where matupás grow in the Amazon basin

Researchers interviewed 45 residents across five communities

Residents report caimans using the islands as nesting ground

Brazil’s Amazon Basin. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

Local folklore ties the islands to a giant anaconda

A landscape hidden in plain sight

In the flooded lakes of the Brazilian Amazon, some rainforest islands have spent their entire lives floating. The trees, which may grow up to 12 meters (about 39 feet) tall, have their root system firmly established in a raft of vegetation that is about 3 meters (approximately 10 feet) deep and floats on the water surface below. Matupás are considered to be important fishing grounds by local communities due to the presence of arapaima, one of the largest freshwater fish species. The local inhabitants also appreciate the fertile soil on the islands, which can be utilized for gardening or growing crops, an idea which had not been documented in the scientific literature until 2015.Scientists in Brazil released a peer-reviewed paper in the journal PLOS ONE in 2015 about the matupa, or Amazon’s floating forests, which had not been studied scientifically enough before. Instead of depending solely on aerial photographs and occasional trips to the islands, the scientists chose to go to the people who had been studying these islands since birth, the riverbank communities.A matupá starts off merely as a collection of aquatic plants entwining themselves and floating on top of the lake surface in the floodplain. However, as time goes by, through decades, this entanglement starts to accumulate sediment and decomposed organic matter, forming a substrate thick enough to allow more complex forms of vegetation to develop from the simpler forms such as grasses and herbs to bushes and finally to complete trees.These islands are able to grow into several hectares in size, with a root ball as deep as 3 meters or 10 feet thick and a forest canopy as high as 12 meters or 40 feet high. Since the whole system is buoyant and not anchored to the lake bed, a matupá rises and falls with the water level, rather than drying out or fully flooding.This type of island is seen in the várzea lakes, which are the nutrient-rich floodplains formed by the white-water rivers carrying sediments from the Andes. It is the flow of such sediments that ensures the fertility of the várzea ecosystems and is also responsible for ensuring that matupás can create the necessary organic substratum required for the trees to grow. The study of this kind was conducted at the Reserve of Sustainable Development of Amanã in the state of Amazonas, where matupás are a familiar element of the environment, as shown by the research published in PLOS ONE in 2015.The research centered on semi-structured interviews with 45 residents across five riverine villages within the Amanã Sustainable Development Reserve. Drawing on residents' extensive firsthand experience, the researchers traced how matupás form, which species live on them, and why they matter to the surrounding communities.One of the most interesting facts that emerged from this survey was the extent to which local wildlife has adapted to the floating islands. Residents described caimans nesting directly on the floating vegetation, since a mature matupá's buoyancy keeps their eggs safe from the flooding that would otherwise submerge a nest on the lakebed.The matupás offer the local population more than just wildlife habitat. Community members regularly dig up the islands' decomposed organic soil for their vegetable patches, with some of the larger, more established matupás sturdy enough to grow crops directly on their surfaces.The matupás also have cultural significance apart from ecological significance among the communities where research was carried out. Some people associate the islands with the story of the cobra grande, an anaconda believed to be living under the waters of the islands, which is locally revered as the spirit protector of the rivers and lakes and considered the mother of the waters. Regardless of whether the islands created this legend or not, it goes to show the extent to which the matupás have become significant within the context of these communities.Though matupás are significant not only for their sheer size but also due to their important role in nature, very little scientific research had been conducted prior to the study in question; this was due to the difficulty associated with investigating them, both through traditional fieldwork and their patchy distribution in distant lakes. As a result of drawing on the riverside communities' knowledge as scientific data, the researchers were able to build a much clearer picture of the life cycle of these floating forests, which spend most of the year adrift on the floodplain's rising and falling waters.
Article Summary: Researchers interviewed 45 residents across five communities within the Amanã Sustainable Development Reserve in the state of Amazonas. They traced how matupás form, which species live on them, and why they matter to the surrounding communities. Matupás are considered to be important fishing grounds by local communities due to the presence of arapaima.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.

This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.

Article Title: From waste tyres to slippers: UK student’s idea takes shape
Article Text:
From waste tyres to slippers: UK student’s idea takes shape

Disclaimer - The above content is non-editorial, and TIL hereby disclaims any and all warranties, expressed or implied, relating to it, and does not guarantee, vouch for or necessarily endorse any of the content.

From discarded tyres to footwear with a purpose, the idea began with a childhood experience. At the age of 10, UK-based student Ahaan Bhatnagar visited rural Africa, where he saw children walking long distances barefoot, often without adequate footwear.Moved by what he witnessed, Ahaan gave away his favourite pair of slippers to a child he met during the visit. The experience stayed with him long after he returned home and eventually became the starting point for a larger idea.As he grew older, Ahaan began exploring how discarded materials could be repurposed to address the lack of affordable, durable footwear. His research led him to waste tyres, which he studied as a potential material for making sturdy slipper soles.The idea brought together two concerns he had encountered separately: the growing problem of tyre waste and the need for accessible footwear.He found skilled craftsmen in Kerala, and with support from HY Estates Limited, an electrically operated machine boosted production to about 160 pairs a day. Ahaan then connected with Mamco General Trading, which operates in Uganda and Zambia. As part of its Corporate Social Responsibility programme, the company will purchase 4,000 pairs of slippers each month for free distribution to children and families in need. It’s a sustainable cycle that turns waste into opportunity, supporting livelihoods and giving kids durable footwear.“When I was 10 years old, I saw children my age walking barefoot, and I never forgot that moment,” Ahaan says. “I wanted to create something that could help people and the environment. If we can turn discarded tyres into something useful and long-lasting, maybe it can inspire more young people to believe their simple ideas can really make a difference.”The world’s growing dependence on convenience and mobility comes with an environmental cost. Every year, more than a billion tyres reach the end of their usable life, creating a significant waste-management challenge. Many of these tyres end up in landfills, while others are burned or processed in ways that can contribute to pollution and the loss of valuable materials.Repurposing discarded tyres offers one way to address this challenge by keeping materials in use for longer and reducing the amount of waste that needs to be disposed of. Turning old tyres into durable slipper soles, for instance, gives a material that would otherwise be discarded a new application while also reducing the need for virgin raw materials in footwear production.The approach reflects a broader shift in how sustainability is being understood. Rather than treating waste simply as something to be collected and discarded, initiatives like this explore how materials already in circulation can be redesigned and put to practical use.In doing so, they can support waste reduction, resource conservation and efforts to lower the environmental impact associated with new production. Ultimately, sustainability is not only about recycling what has already been used, but also about rethinking waste as a potential resource.
Article Summary: UK-based student Ahaan Bhatnagar saw children walking barefoot in rural Africa. His research led him to waste tyres, which he studied as a potential material for making sturdy slipper soles. He found skilled craftsmen in Kerala and with support from HY Estates Limited, an electrically operated machine boosted production to about 160 pairs a day.

Article Title: Apple CEO John Ternus on the most profound change at iPhone maker over the last 20 years: ‘ Top of the list, of course…’
Article Text:
Apple CEO John Ternus

Custom Silicon at the ‘Top of the List’

Apple's approach to product development has shifted dramatically over the past two decades, moving away from designing hardware around off-the-shelf components and toward building proprietary technology entirely from the ground up. A video of John Ternus from 2023 has resurfaced online, in which the Apple CEO – who was senior vice president of hardware engineering at that time – is seen reflecting on one of the most significant shifts the iPhone maker has undergone over the last 20 years. In the 2023 interview with CNBC, Ternus pointed to the aggressive push toward in-house engineering as the defining strategic shift of the modern era. He said that above all proprietary technology, custom Apple silicon tops the list.“When I started, the way we tended to make products was we were using technologies from other companies and we were effectively building the product around that. We made these beautiful products, but they were constrained by what was available,” Ternus can be seen saying.While that approach produced iconic consumer devices, it placed hard technical ceilings on what hardware teams could build, as per Ternus. That external dependence has steadily disappeared over the last twenty years as Apple brought critical component architectures, like silicon and modems, inside its own laboratories.“One of the most - if not the most - profound changes at Apple over the last 20 years is how we now do so many of the technologies in-house. Top of the list, of course, is our silicon, which as Johnny said from the very beginning, we're thinking about how these pieces are going to come together to make the best possible product for our customers,” Tetanus said.By designing processors tailored exclusively for its own operating systems and device chassis, Apple has moved over earlier hardware limitations, giving designers and engineers full control over performance, efficiency and system integration.Recently, Apple launched the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max powered by Apple A20 Pro, an advanced 2-nanometer mobile chip that has been built by TSMC, features a 6-core CPU configuration and 7-core GPU processor.
Article Summary: Apple CEO John Ternus was senior vice president of hardware engineering at that time. He said that above all proprietary technology, custom Apple silicon tops the list. The aggressive push toward in-house engineering is the defining strategic shift of the modern era.

Article Text:

BenQ showcased its MOBIUZ gaming monitor line-up at Tokyo Game Show 2026 held at Makuhari Messe from September 17 to 20, under the theme, "MOBIUZ Game Art Museum.” The theme centres on how MOBIUZ monitors reproduce the work of game creators through this colour tuning, treating each title's visual identity as something to be faithfully rendered rather than simply displayed.At the heart of this year's showcase is Game Art Color HDR, a new firmware feature that builds on BenQ's existing Smart Game Art technology. The feature introduces three HDR presets (Immersive, Balanced and Vivid) for each game art colour mode, giving players finer control over how a title's colour palette and contrast are reproduced on screen. It is available across BenQ's three premium OLED models (EX271UZ, EX321UZ, EX271QZ) and three of its latest QHD models (EX271QMZ, EX271QM, EX271QP), six displays in all.Rajeev Singh, Managing Director, BenQ India and South Asia, said, “Gaming today is as much about a title's visual identity as it is about performance, and Indian gamers are increasingly discerning about both. As India's gaming and esports audience continues to grow, this is the kind of display innovation we’re bringing closer to our market.Speaking on the BenQ MOBIUZ range, Jeffrey Liang, President, BenQ Asia Pacific, said, "The Game Art Museum concept is really about how closely we work with game creators on colour science. Game Art Color HDR is a direct result of that: it lets a monitor read a title's art direction and respond to it. As APAC becomes one of the fastest-growing regions for PC and console gaming, that kind of art-led engineering is what will differentiate MOBIUZ as the category matures. ”Beyond the display wall, the Tokyo booth gave visitors a dedicated area to compare each model's performance side by side, and a hands-on zone to try anticipated game titles in MOBIUZ's flagship setup. This ran alongside exhibits featuring game developers speaking to their own creative choices around visuals and world-building, the same choices Game Art Color HDR is built to reproduce on screen.

Article Title: Microsoft says it has taken down ‘AI chatbot built for cybercrime’ that hacked 12,000-plus emails across over 10,000 organisations globally
Article Text:
Targets in several countries, including India

How the scam actually worked

Microsoft has said that it has thwarted an effort to shut down a subscription-based scam platform that relied on an AI chatbot to break into more than 12,000 Microsoft accounts over the course of a few months. The platform, called EvilTokens, first surfaced on a Telegram channel back in February, charging users an initial fee of $1,500 followed by a recurring monthly charge of $500. EvilTokens essentially offered a one-stop service that streamlined nearly every step needed to compromise email accounts at scale. According to the company, once inside, the platform helped its customers sift through victims' inboxes, identify the most targets and even draft follow-up emails designed to trick employees into transferring funds into accounts controlled by the attackers.“In short, AI was not simply helping attackers write more convincing messages. It helped them decide who to target, who to impersonate, and how to most effectively exploit the relationship to extract as much money as possible,” the company said.Microsoft says that while it also attacked specific countries, its significance extends beyond its rapid growth and global reach.“Microsoft observed the highest concentrations of victim activity in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia, India, and France.Affected organizations ranged from wholesale distribution and construction to financial services, real estate, higher education, and healthcare. Working with partners, Microsoft seized 50 websites used to operate the service and disabled more than 150 additional domains tied to its supporting infrastructure. In the United Kingdom, the Metropolitan Police Service’s cybercrime team arrested two men on suspicion of offenses connected with the alleged operation of EvilTokens,” the company said.According to Microsoft, what set EvilTokens apart was the AI-style chatbot sitting at the heart of the operation. The chatbot could analyse a victim's inbox and help criminals pinpoint trusted relationships, payment approval authority, sensitive job responsibilities and other circumstances where fraud was most likely to succeed. It could even go a step further, recommending specific fraud strategies and drafting messages impersonating trusted contacts to manipulate victims into taking action.The account compromises were carried out through a legitimate OAuth authentication process known as device code authentication. This method was originally designed for devices like smart TVs, essentially anything lacking a standard login interface. In this setup, the device being signed into displays a code, and the user is instructed to enter that code into a browser on a separate device, which then gets authenticated.EvilTokens gave its customers a platform capable of automating the mass sending of spam emails. Anyone who clicked on a malicious link or attachment inside these emails would be redirected to a webpage running a hidden automation script, which interacted in real time with the victim's Microsoft identity provider to generate a device code that would enrol a device belonging to the attacker.The victim would then see this device code onscreen, along with instructions telling them to copy it and enter it into Microsoft's official device login portal. Behind the scenes, complex backend operations allowed the hackers slip past traditional signature- or pattern-based security detection systems. This technique powered the entire attack chain, from generating dynamic device codes all the way through to actions taken after an account was compromised.Microsoft said EvilTokens marks a significant shift in how mass account compromises, and everything that follows them, now unfold.
Article Summary: Microsoft says it has thwarted an effort to shut down a subscription-based scam platform that relied on an AI chatbot. The platform, called EvilTokens, first surfaced on a Telegram channel back in February, charging users an initial fee of $1,500 followed by a recurring monthly charge of $500. According to the company, once inside, the platform helped its customers sift through victims' inboxes, identify the most targets and even draft follow-up emails.

Article Title: Adobe Premiere mobile app now available on Android: What it means for users
Article Text:
“Today, we’re excited to share that Adobe Premiere on mobile is now available on Android for free”,

“With 95% of Indian creators already being mobile-first, the smartphone is fast becoming the studio for India’s next generation of creators. Adobe Premiere mobile Android availability

Adobe Premiere mobile app : Key features

More features coming to Adobe Premiere mobile app

Adobe has expanded its Premiere mobile video editing app to Android, bringing it to a wider range of users after launching it on iPhone last year. It also offers frame-accurate editing and a multi-track timeline that lets users layer video, music, text, and effects.Users can also start projects with creator-made templates or create their own. The app includes effects, transitions, creative assets, and music from Adobe Stock, plus the ability to use files stored on the device or extract audio from videos.Adobe Premiere mobile supports editing and exporting videos at up to 4K. Adobe says the app does not require a forced login or show upgrade prompts during editing.The app also includes generative AI features powered by Adobe Firefly. These include Generative Fill, Image-to-Video and Generate Sound Effects. Adobe says the mobile experience is also ad-free and does not add a watermark to edited videos.Adobe says it plans to add more features to the mobile app, including Adobe Fonts, enhanced captions, keyframes, cropping, beat detection and continued editing between Premiere mobile and Premiere on desktop. The free version includes the core video editing tools, while additional generative credits and storage are available through upgrades.Adobe has also shared feedback from creators using Premiere mobile. Adhiraj Singh Anand said Enhance Audio helps him clean up sound after recording in uncontrolled environments, while Mohanraj Thangaraj said he uses the app to edit drone, camera and phone footage into short-form videos while travelling.Katarina Mogus highlighted the app's YouTube Shorts templates for creating and publishing videos while on the go. Vimal Sharma said the Android version gives him access to video editing tools, including sound enhancement and frame-level control, without needing a laptop.
Article Summary: Adobe has expanded its Premiere mobile video editing app to Android. The Android version is free and includes tools for editing video, audio, effects, and other content. The app supports video editing and export at up to 4K resolution, along with a multi-track timeline.

Article Title: Employees at OpenAI, Anthropic and other top AI companies complain of mental strain over working on …
Article Text:
Mental stress no limited to evaluation companies

Bioterror and cyber vulnerabilities spark growing alarm

Employees working at leading artificial intelligence (AI) labs and evaluation companies are reportedly facing increasing mental distress, driven by fears that the powerful software they are engineering may inflict widespread harm on society. At the UK’s AI Security Institute (Aisi), which is regarded globally as a leading independent evaluation center for frontier models, multiple staff members have taken stress leave and entered counseling, The Financial Times reported, citing individuals familiar with the matter. Further, the publication reported that compressed evaluation timelines for unreleased software, paired with unease over rapid commercial deployments have led to burnout and deteriorating morale inside the agency.Similar reports have come out from major tech companies, including OpenAI , Anthropic and Google DeepMind, where several specialists have resigned after concluding their projects carry excessive societal danger.The report notes that a Google DeepMind staffer described the effort to establish safety safeguards as an uphill battle that feels like an impossible task, noting that working on AI carries the strain of not knowing how deployments will ultimately be utilised.The worker cited Google’s April agreement granting the US Department of Defense (DOD) access to its systems for classified defense applications as a major source of internal tension.“So many people are upset, there have been various quittings and a lot of mental health leave. Partly this feeling of being out of control, and also that you’re building something that is causing real damage,” the employee was quoted as saying.Insiders argue that these workplace stresses stem from corporate rivalry and management decisions, complicated by the introduction of autonomous systems into sensitive domains like power grids and conflict zones without adequate legal or commercial boundaries, The Financial Times report added.Some specialists monitoring cybersecurity and biochemistry have voiced concern following sudden advances in algorithmic capabilities, including systems capable of uncovering zero-day software exploits or designing novel biological pathogens. A former Aisi researcher described an atmosphere of pervasive dread within testing teams:“There is this sense that reckless things are being embedded in how tech is released and that is not changing. There is constant anxiety from people who are saying, can anything stop this, or are we watching the world burn?”Responding to the concerns, official bodies and research firms maintained that employee care programs remain active.The UK Government stated that while frontier technological testing is demanding and fast-paced, employee wellbeing and manageable workflows remain central to Aisi's operations, with support services open to affected personnel.Google DeepMind, which is the AI unit of Google, acknowledged the high-intensity nature of advanced research, asserting that worker wellness resources, formal avenues to escalate safety concerns, and direct communication channels with executive leadership remain top priorities.Recently, Jacob Coxon, a 27-year-old researcher, who previously worked at both OpenAI and Anthropic, resigned publicly this month while accusing top labs of gambling with human survival.Mrinank Sharma, Anthropic safety specialist focusing on mitigating AI-enabled bioterrorism left in February, cautioning in a departure note that the world faces severe peril.Hieu Pham, formerly with OpenAI and Elon Musk’s xAI, Pham stepped down earlier this year to return to Vietnam, writing candidly about the severe toll of advanced model development.
Article Summary: Employees at leading AI labs and evaluation companies are reportedly facing increasing mental distress, driven by fears that the powerful software they are engineering may inflict widespread harm on society. At the UK’s AI Security Institute (Aisi), multiple staff members have taken stress leave and entered counseling.
